key_insight: An incremental Deep Energy Method couples history-dependent plasticity and plasticity-dependent fracture toughness using separate displacement and phase-field representations.
engineering_relevance: The framework models plastic deformation and crack propagation together, supporting computational assessment of ductile failure in elasto-plastic solids.
method: Couple second-order Ambrosio–Tortorelli fracture with small-strain J2 plasticity, linear isotropic hardening and local radial-return updates.
Alternately minimise energy using a ReZero displacement network and localised Gaussian radial basis functions for the phase field.
Reuse trainable parameters and optimiser states across load increments while carrying constitutive history separately at quadrature points.
evidence_signal: Numerical results show close agreement with finite-element references for force–displacement responses, energy evolution, plastic deformation and crack propagation.
watch_item: Accuracy becomes more sensitive to loading-increment size near abrupt fracture events.
paper_title: A deep energy method formulation for phase-field modelling of ductile fracture
